Formulation  
Patient with a history of anxiety currently managed on Sertraline presents with new onset unilateral headache with some photophobia and associated work-related stress. Headache likely tension-type or migraine exacerbated by stress, fatigue, and possible suboptimal sleep and hydration. Work stress and anxiety act as precipitating and perpetuating factors, with protective factors including partner support and medication adherence.

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Headache (Tension-type vs. Migraine)  
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce headache frequency and severity; improve comfort and functioning  
- Clinical Goal(s): Symptom relief; identification and management of contributing stressors  
- Actions (Patient): Take Ibuprofen as advised; continue Paracetamol if needed; increase hydration to 1.5–2 liters daily; improve sleep hygiene aiming for 7-8 hours sleep; consider taking time off work to reduce stress; self-refer for counselling  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Prescribe Ibuprofen with dosing appropriate for migraine; provide pain management advice; provide counselling service referral information; advise on lifestyle modifications; arrange follow-up in 1 week; monitor for worsening or new symptoms; provide educational materials on headache warning signs  

Secondary Problem: Anxiety Disorder (Stable, on Sertraline)  
- Patient Goal(s): Maintain anxiety control; reduce work-related anxiety episodes  
- Clinical Goal(s): Prevent anxiety exacerbation; provide access to counselling to address stress  
- Actions (Patient): Continue Sertraline as prescribed; engage with counselling services; monitor anxiety levels and triggers  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Review Sertraline adherence at follow-up; support referral to counselling; assess anxiety at next appointment  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes. Topics covered: headache types, managing stress, medication use, hydration, sleep hygiene, warning signs for serious headache symptoms  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increasing headache severity, new neurological symptoms, persistent nausea/vomiting, worsening anxiety or mood changes  
- Coping Strategies: Sleep hygiene, hydration, pacing work demands, counselling support
